framings.label: Neutral production announcement
framings.description: Reports the wind-down as a straightforward corporate news item, citing Musk's statement and the timing (Texas, 2027) without evaluative language.

framings.label: Commercial flop and weak sales
framings.description: Frames the end of the Cybertruck as the result of poor demand, citing sales far below plan, limited markets and a polarizing design, often with words like 'flop' or 'failure'.

framings.label: Strategic pivot to Cybercab and AI
framings.description: Presents the wind-down as a reallocation of factory capacity and company focus toward Cybercab, robotaxis, robotics and AI.

framings.label: Quality and recall troubles
framings.description: Looks back at the truck's problems, such as cracked windows, delays and repeated recalls, as part of its troubled record.

framings.label: Obituary and skeptical commentary
framings.description: Uses eulogy-style or pointed language ('RIP', 'Is Dead', 'convenient excuse') to treat the end as a symbolic moment or to question Musk's stated reasons.
